prompt: Required researcher: prochatgpt_researcher. Conduct a focused, evidence-backed clinical and regulatory audit for people with lipedema who also have edema or a condition for which a diuretic may be prescribed. Do not operate a browser UI manually and do not treat snippets, SEO clinics, supplement sellers, or ChatGPT claims as evidence. Separate direct lipedema evidence from adjacent evidence. Compare loop diuretics, thiazide/thiazide-like agents, mineralocorticoid-receptor antagonists and other potassium-sparing agents, acetazolamide, and SGLT2 inhibitors when patients mistakenly call them “water pills.” Determine which phenotypes (heart failure, kidney disease, cirrhosis, hypertension, venous disease, lymphatic disease, idiopathic/orthostatic edema, and pure lipedema) have guideline-supported indications or lack of benefit. Audit deprescribing/withdrawal evidence, rebound versus recurrence of the underlying disease, neurohormonal adaptation, monitoring, and red flags, but do not invent a taper or give individualized dosing. Prioritize current ESC/AHA/KDIGO/EASL/AEMPS/EMA/ISL/S2k or comparable primary guidance, systematic reviews and trials, with dates, populations, limitations, and conflicts. Explicitly verify whether a lipedema-specific diuretic trial exists. Search Spanish/European regulatory material and product information where relevant. Return opened URLs/PMIDs/DOIs, exact claims supported, contradictions, what is safe to say on a plain-language Spanish website, and a short falsation section targeting “diuretics always worsen lipedema,” “MRA/SGLT2 are only water loss,” and “any post-withdrawal swelling is rebound.” Mark inaccessible sources and uncertainty; no marketing or unsupported cure claims.
